headline: Anderlecht have no Europa League points and are still the favourites
summary: Anderlecht arrive in Białystok with 0 points in the Europa League and a Belgian Cup exit behind them, beaten 1-2 at Beerschot on Sunday. They sit 29th of 36. And yet the market still makes them favourites, at 42.7% to win. The reason is Jagiellonia: four defeats in their last five matches, 1.88 expected goals conceded per game, and one of their most-used defenders, Wojtuszek, out after 759 minutes this season. Over 2.75 goals is priced at 48.8%, so chances at both ends. The market rates Anderlecht only 0.25 goals better — a close game.
read: Jagiellonia have lost four of their last five and concede 1.88 xG per game, and the goal line sits at 2.75 with the over just short of even money.

facts.fact: Anderlecht are the favourites at 42.7% to win in Białystok, ahead of Jagiellonia at 30.7%.
facts.meaning: The market makes Anderlecht more likely than not to avoid defeat, but nowhere near a certainty — this is a narrow away favourite.

facts.fact: Anderlecht have zero points from their two Europa League games, losing 1-2 at home to Lyon and 0-1 away to Dinamo Zagreb, and sit 29th of 36.
facts.meaning: A third straight European defeat would leave them with almost nothing to play for in the league phase.

facts.fact: Anderlecht were knocked out of the Belgian Cup on Sunday, losing 1-2 at Beerschot; coach Vitor Bruno said afterwards: 'I don't see the situation like that' when asked about a crisis.
facts.meaning: A cup exit three days before a European away trip puts the spotlight on the coach and on a squad that has now lost two in a row.

facts.fact: Jagiellonia lost 0-1 at Zagłębie Lubin on Saturday, conceding a VAR-awarded Sebastian Kerk penalty.
facts.meaning: Their domestic slump is the backdrop to this game: they arrive with one win in their last five matches.

facts.fact: Jagiellonia have conceded 1.88 expected goals per game across their last five matches.
facts.meaning: They give up real chances even when the scoreline looks respectable — Anderlecht's forward line should get looks in Białystok.

facts.fact: The Asian handicap fair line is +0.25 to Jagiellonia — the market rates Anderlecht only about a quarter of a goal better.
facts.meaning: This is a coin-flip match with a slight away tilt; nothing in the pricing points to an Anderlecht rout.

facts.fact: Over 2.75 goals is priced at 48.8% — the market leans just under three goals.
facts.meaning: A game with chances at both ends, but the market stops short of expecting a shootout.

facts.fact: Jagiellonia are without defender Norbert Wojtuszek, who has played 759 minutes this season.
facts.meaning: One of their most-used defensive players is missing exactly where the numbers say they are weakest.

sources.fact: Jagiellonia lost 1-0 to Zagłębie Lubin on October 18, conceding a VAR-awarded Sebastian Kerk penalty in the 77th minute.
Rodrigo Conceiçao, who has played for Jagiellonia since last summer, scored in the Europa League last week.
Jagiellonia coach Adrian Siemieniec was suspended for six matches in the Polish league after a scandal, but he will still be able to sit on the bench against Anderlecht.
Jagiellonia have their first Europa League points, having beaten Ararat-Armenia in the previous round.
Polish media note that Jagiellonia have had problems recently, especially domestically, with the 0-1 defeat to Zagłębie Lubin cited.
Anderlecht have yet to earn a point in this season's Europa League, losing 1-2 at home to Olympique Lyon and 0-1 away to Dinamo Zagreb.
Defender Giulian Biancone, a doubt, is set to return to action in Białystok after training with the squad that travelled to Poland.
Vitor Bruno said at his pre-match press conference: "I was not born mauve but I am in love with the club" and promised a good Anderlecht performance in Poland.

disclaimer: 18+ · Market analysis, not betting advice. Probabilities are the market's, with the margin removed.
